answer: Cross-epoch behaviour ledger scoring. Each identity's actions are scored against its own prior-epoch distribution, so a farmed cluster must sustain the same distinct signature across many rounds to avoid a ledge penalty that zeroes its score. Divergent clones get pruned when their timing and interaction graph drift from the cohort's meadow of normal variance. Maintaining that consistency costs an attacker sustained compute and coordination per identity, a poor haven versus cheap one-shot creation.
